To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vitamin D deficiency is associated with an increased risk of developing type 1 diabetes in genetically susceptible children.

the vitamin A status of the children in the study was determined by the isotope dilution method, the serum retinol concentration was used to assess vitamin A status, and the vitamin A status was found to be low.

the use of the 24-hour dietary recall and 24-hour urine collection methods in the study population resulted in a large number of missing data and a large amount of variability in nutrient intake and excretion, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the determination of the concentration of retinol in blood serum.

the development of new methods for the analysis of the chemical composition and physical properties of food products and with the development of methods of processing food products in order to improve their quality and safety, to extend their shelf life and to reduce their production cost.
the development of a method for the determination of the vitamin A content of foods and feeds, and with the use of the results of these determinations to assess the adequacy of vitamin A intake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vitamin A deficiency is associated with increased risk of death from all causes and with increased risk of diarrheal disease and measles in young children.
the use of serum retinol concentrations as an indicator of vitamin A status in children is not appropriate.
the use of serum retinol concentrations to assess vitamin A status is not recommended.

Serum retinols concentrations demonstrate high specificity but questionable sensitivity compared to liver stores calculated from isotopic dilution in determining Vitamin A deficiency in Thai & Zambian children
Serum retinyl palmitate concentrations demonstrate high specificity and sensitivity compared with liver vitamin A stores calculated from isotopically diluting deuterated retinyl palimitate (D-RP) in determining Vitamin A status in Thai children.
the serum retinol concentration (SROC) and the isotope dilution method are both valid indicators of vitamin A status in children.
we have shown the following in our two studies: 1) serum retinol is highly specific for vitamin A status, but 2) the sensitivity of serum retinol as a marker is limited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vitamin A deficiency is still prevalent in many parts of the world and is a significant problem.
the liver is a major source of vitamin A for the body and is an important reservoir.
we need to do more to understand and address the social determinants of health.
